So I wanted to create something for people to read when looking into programming. This guide isn't aimed at teaching you anything to do with programming but more about how to learn and become a better coder. I'm by no means myself a great coder but these tips have helped me so much with learning programming and I think they may help other as well.

  1. Pick an intermediate programming language --- More often than not I see people jumping into a language such as C++ with no programming knowledge what so ever and this is a big mistake. You'll likely be overwhelmed by advanced programming languages and are more likely to give up. So what language should you learn? Well a great starting point is something like Java or C# but it also does depend on what type of programming you want to do, such as web development, games, servers/databases etc. I highly recommend these 2 languages as they are not overly simple but not overly difficult and it should give you a good starting point to your programming career. Universities teach these languages for a reason and they are used so much in the commercial world.

  2. Practice practice practice --- It doesn't matter how many hours you spend reading or watching videos, you need to practice and not just copy what you have seen. You need to make sure you expand on what you see, try combining new topics with what you have already learnt and really push yourself to learn as much as you can. I personally learnt game development by learning what I needed as I built my first game.

  3. You never really stop learning --- I've seen this before. You're new to programming, excited and looking forward to mastering the language... this is highly unlikely. Programming languages have so much content and you will likely never learn everything and will always be learning new things. Programming is not something you learn and then simply never learn about again, you need dedication and must enjoying learning new topics to enjoy coding.

  4. Time --- You will not become a great programmer overnight, It's going to be hard work and you need to really enjoy it. If you're finding yourself losing interest in programming maybe try a new language or start a new project. Programmers lose motivation all the time, I recently suffered myself but once I had a little break for a few weeks, I felt much better.

  5. The first language is the hardest --- You're going to be new to a whole wide world and trust me, the first language is going to be the hardest. Once you learn a language you will be able to pick up others a lot faster and you will love using a wide range of languages.

  6. Don't limit yourself to one language! --- A good programmer knows a wide range of different languages. I limited myself for far to long to Java and I wish I had started branching to different languages sooner. I'm currently learning C# and Javascript and loving it! It's great to be able to do things in different languages.

  7. Have fun --- If you're not enjoying programming you need to ask yourself why. Make sure you find a language you love, you might not like the first language you code in. I personally dislike web development (so so much) but I'm learning it for University and because employers love programmers who can code in a range of languages. If you're having fun you're more likely to learn!

So... Where can you learn to program for free? Well the internet is the best place. You have a wide range of sites at your finger tips and below I've listed some useful links for different languages.
